speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and cutaneous).

Thank you for providing those details. Given your age, significant smoking history, African origin, and the presence of non-healing, crusted lesions on both the penis and an acral site that failed previous treatments, these findings are highly suspicious for malignancy. I would like to confirm this with a biopsy. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_of_penile_lesion and Biopsy_of_finger_lesion. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy_of_penile_lesion and Dermoscopy_of_finger_lesion.
